scales.name: Major
scales.description: The major scale is the foundation of Western harmony. Its pattern of whole and half steps creates the familiar bright sound heard in countless melodies.
scales.tip: Listen for the half steps between degrees 3–4 and 7–8. They give the major scale its pull toward home.

scales.name: Natural Minor
scales.description: Natural minor lowers the 3rd, 6th and 7th degrees of the major scale. The lowered 3rd is the note that most clearly creates its minor character.
scales.tip: Compare it with major and focus on degree 3. That single change immediately shifts the emotional color.

scales.name: Harmonic Minor
scales.description: Harmonic minor raises the 7th degree of natural minor. This creates a strong leading tone back to the root and a distinctive large step between degrees 6 and 7.
scales.tip: Hear how the raised 7th wants to resolve upward to the root. That tension is why this minor works so well in harmony.

scales.name: Melodic Minor
scales.description: Ascending melodic minor keeps the minor 3rd but raises degrees 6 and 7. It smooths the melodic gaps found in harmonic minor while preserving a strong return to the root.
scales.tip: This finder uses the ascending form. Classical melodies often use natural minor again when descending.

scales.name: Major Pentatonic
scales.description: Major pentatonic removes the two most tense notes from the major scale. Its five-note shape is easy to sing and appears across many musical traditions.
scales.tip: Because it avoids half steps, almost every note sits comfortably over a major chord.

scales.name: Minor Pentatonic
scales.description: Minor pentatonic condenses the natural minor sound into five strong notes. It is central to rock, blues, pop and improvisation.
scales.tip: Start and end phrases on the root, then lean on the minor 3rd to make the scale's character unmistakable.

scales.name: Blues
scales.description: The blues scale adds a chromatic flat 5th to minor pentatonic. That passing blue note creates tension that sounds best when it moves to a neighboring note.
scales.tip: Do not camp on the blue note at first—slide through it toward degree 4 or 5.

scales.name: Dorian
scales.description: Dorian is a minor mode with a raised 6th. That brighter 6th separates it from natural minor and gives it an energetic, forward-moving quality.
scales.tip: Emphasize the natural 6th over a minor chord to reveal the Dorian sound.
